# Version lock for the deployed webapp — generated by pip freeze from the
# known-green development venv at the commit below. Applied by deploy/deploy.sh
# as `pip install -c constraints.txt -e '.[web,pdf,dev]'` so a server install
# resolves the SAME versions the test suite was green against, instead of
# whatever is newest on PyPI the day of the deploy.
#
# This is a CONSTRAINTS file, not a requirements file: it pins versions but
# installs nothing. pyproject.toml still declares what gets installed; a pin
# here for a package that is not a dependency is simply ignored.
#
# Generated:      2026-07-30 03:14 UTC
# Source commit:  17a8679
# Python:         3.12.7 (Ubuntu 24.04's python3-venv is 3.12 — matched)
# Platform:       generated on darwin; verified free of platform-only pins.
#                 uvloop/httptools/watchfiles/pillow/cffi all ship manylinux wheels.
#
# To refresh: re-run pip freeze --exclude-editable in a green venv and replace
# the block below. --exclude-editable matters — pip REJECTS an editable (-e)
# line in a constraints file, and a plain freeze includes this project itself.
#
# SEC-1 hand-edit (2026-09-05) — the ONE line in this file not from a freeze:
#   pypdf 6.14.2 -> 6.16.1
# pip-audit reported six advisories against 6.14.2 (PYSEC-2026-3655, -3656,
# CVE-2026-84309, -84310, -84311, -82398); 6.16.1 fixes all six. pypdf is
# declared in no extra and required by no installed package, so nothing ever
# installs it from this project — the pin was a ghost of the dev venv this file
# was frozen from, and only tests/ and scripts/ import it. KEEP THE BUMP when
# regenerating: a plain re-freeze from a stale venv would silently reintroduce
# the vulnerable pin and turn .github/workflows/security.yml red.

# PREFLIP-1 hand-additions (2026-09-11) — eight lines, also not from a freeze,
# closing precondition A1 (docs/checkpoint4-preconditions.md). deploy/deploy.sh
# now installs `.[web,pdf,dev,db,auth]`, so for the first time a deploy resolves
# SQLAlchemy, Alembic, Authlib and a Postgres driver, and an unpinned resolve is
# the thing this file exists to prevent:
#
#   alembic==1.19.2        SQLAlchemy==2.0.52     Authlib==1.8.0
#   psycopg==3.3.5         psycopg-binary==3.3.5
#   Mako==1.4.1            cryptography==50.0.1   joserfc==1.7.5
#
# The last three are NOT named by precondition A1 and are pinned anyway: they
# are the transitive closure the two extras newly pull in (alembic -> Mako,
# Authlib -> cryptography + joserfc). Pinning only the four the precondition
# names would leave three packages floating on a file whose whole purpose is
# that "a server install resolves the SAME versions the test suite was green
# against" — a constraints file with holes in it is a version lock that reports
# success and does not hold.
#
# MEASURED, not chosen: each is `pip freeze --exclude-editable` in the dev venv
# at this commit, after `pip install '.[web,pdf,dev,db,auth]'`. psycopg was not
# in that venv at all — it had never been installed on this machine — so it was
# installed first and then read, rather than picked off PyPI's front page.
#
# psycopg AND psycopg-binary, two lines for one dependency: `psycopg[binary]`
# resolves to both distributions, and constraining only the first leaves the
# compiled wheel — the half that actually talks to the database — unpinned.
#
# The SEC-1 warning above applies to these too, and harder: a plain re-freeze of
# a venv that lacks the [db]/[auth] extras will DELETE all eight of these lines
# and the deploy will silently go back to resolving whatever PyPI has that day.
